import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length4_82/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length4_82/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length4_82/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length4_82/training_3.csv", index_col=0)
source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length4_82/training_4.csv", index_col=0)

# Step 1: Join Source4_82_0 and Source4_82_1 on Institution
# Note: Source0 has columns ['Institution', 'year 2016']
#       Source1 has columns ['Institution', 'year 2014']
# The intermediate_step1 schema shows columns like '(Fall 2011)', '(Fall 2012)', etc. are present,
# but source0 and source1 do not have those columns.
# This suggests that the intermediate_step1 was produced by joining source0 and source1 and then
# renaming or adding columns from somewhere else.
# However, from the prompt, the first operation is JOIN [["Source4_82_0", "Source4_82_1"], ["Institution", "Institution"]].
# We will join source0 and source1 on Institution, then rename year columns to persist columns as per target schema.

df_01 = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="Institution", how="outer")

# Rename year columns to match target persist columns:
# From source1: 'year 2014' -> 'persist 2014'
# From source0: 'year 2016' -> 'persist 2016'
# We also have 'persist 2015' in target, which is from source3 (year 2015)
df_01.rename(columns={"year 2014": "persist 2014", "year 2016": "persist 2016"}, inplace=True)

# Step 2: Join Source4_82_2 and Source4_82_4 on Institution
# Source2 has many '(Fall YYYY)' columns including '(Fall 2011)' to '(Fall 2014)'
# Source4 has 'Cohort 2014', 'Cohort 2015', 'Cohort 2016'
df_24 = pd.merge(source2, source4, on="Institution", how="outer")

# Step 3: Join Source4_82_0 and Source4_82_4 on Institution
# This join is to get year 2016 and cohort columns together
df_04 = pd.merge(source0, source4, on="Institution", how="outer")

# Now, to produce the final target table Target4_82 with schema:
# ['Institution': string,
#  '(Fall 2011)': float,
#  '(Fall 2012)': float,
#  '(Fall 2013)': float,
#  '(Fall 2014)': float,
#  'persist 2014': integer,
#  'persist 2015': integer,
#  'persist 2016': integer,
#  'Cohort 2014': integer,
#  'Cohort 2015': integer,
#  'Cohort 2016': integer]

# We have:
# - '(Fall 2011)' to '(Fall 2014)' from df_24 (source2)
# - 'persist 2014' from df_01 (source1)
# - 'persist 2015' from source3 (year 2015)
# - 'persist 2016' from df_01 (source0)
# - 'Cohort 2014', 'Cohort 2015', 'Cohort 2016' from df_24 or df_04 (both have cohorts)

# We need to combine all these pieces together on Institution.

# First, rename source3 'year 2015' to 'persist 2015'
source3_renamed = source3.rename(columns={"year 2015": "persist 2015"})

# Merge df_01 and source3_renamed on Institution to get persist 2014, persist 2015, persist 2016 together
df_persist = pd.merge(df_01, source3_renamed[["Institution", "persist 2015"]], on="Institution", how="outer")

# Merge df_persist with df_24 to get Fall columns and Cohort columns
df_final = pd.merge(df_persist, df_24[["Institution", "(Fall 2011)", "(Fall 2012)", "(Fall 2013)", "(Fall 2014)",
                                      "Cohort 2014", "Cohort 2015", "Cohort 2016"]], on="Institution", how="outer")

# Ensure columns are in the target order
target_columns = ['Institution', '(Fall 2011)', '(Fall 2012)', '(Fall 2013)', '(Fall 2014)',
                  'persist 2014', 'persist 2015', 'persist 2016',
                  'Cohort 2014', 'Cohort 2015', 'Cohort 2016']

# Some columns might be missing due to outer joins, fill them with NaN or appropriate types
for col in target_columns:
    if col not in df_final.columns:
        df_final[col] = pd.NA

df_final = df_final[target_columns]

# Convert types to match target schema:
# Institution: string
df_final['Institution'] = df_final['Institution'].astype(str)

# '(Fall YYYY)': float
for col in ['(Fall 2011)', '(Fall 2012)', '(Fall 2013)', '(Fall 2014)']:
    df_final[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_final[col], errors='coerce')

# 'persist YYYY' and 'Cohort YYYY': integer (nullable Int64 to allow NaNs)
for col in ['persist 2014', 'persist 2015', 'persist 2016', 'Cohort 2014', 'Cohort 2015', 'Cohort 2016']:
    df_final[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_final[col], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# Save the final dataframe to the target path
df_final.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_82/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_82/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_82/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_82/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_82/training_3.csv", index_col=0)
source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_82/training_4.csv", index_col=0)

# Join source2 (dimension table with many columns) with each of the other sources on 'Institution'
df = source2.merge(source0, on="Institution", how="inner")
df = df.merge(source1, on="Institution", how="inner")
df = df.merge(source3, on="Institution", how="inner")
df = df.merge(source4, on="Institution", how="inner")

# The target schema has these columns:
# ['Institution': string, '(Fall 2011)': float, '(Fall 2012)': float, '(Fall 2013)': float, '(Fall 2014)': float,
#  'persist 2014': integer, 'persist 2015': integer, 'persist 2016': integer,
#  'Cohort 2014': integer, 'Cohort 2015': integer, 'Cohort 2016': integer]

# The persist columns come from year 2014, 2015, 2016 columns in source0, source3, source1 respectively
# But source0 has 'year 2016', source1 has 'year 2014', source3 has 'year 2015'
# We need to rename these to 'persist 2016', 'persist 2014', 'persist 2015' respectively

# Rename year columns to persist columns
df = df.rename(columns={
    'year 2014': 'persist 2014',
    'year 2015': 'persist 2015',
    'year 2016': 'persist 2016'
})

# The Cohort columns are already in source4 as 'Cohort 2014', 'Cohort 2015', 'Cohort 2016'

# Select only the columns needed in the target schema
cols = ['Institution', '(Fall 2011)', '(Fall 2012)', '(Fall 2013)', '(Fall 2014)',
        'persist 2014', 'persist 2015', 'persist 2016',
        'Cohort 2014', 'Cohort 2015', 'Cohort 2016']

df = df[cols]

# The persist and Cohort columns are floats due to merge, convert them to integers
for col in ['persist 2014', 'persist 2015', 'persist 2016', 'Cohort 2014', 'Cohort 2015', 'Cohort 2016']:
    df[col] = df[col].astype(int)

# Group by Institution to ensure uniqueness and sum aggregation on integer columns
df = df.groupby('Institution', as_index=False).agg({
    '(Fall 2011)': 'first',
    '(Fall 2012)': 'first',
    '(Fall 2013)': 'first',
    '(Fall 2014)': 'first',
    'persist 2014': 'sum',
    'persist 2015': 'sum',
    'persist 2016': 'sum',
    'Cohort 2014': 'sum',
    'Cohort 2015': 'sum',
    'Cohort 2016': 'sum'
})

# Write output to the target file
df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_82/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
